subject: Physics
curriculumBasis: Curated chapter-level simulations based on NCERT/CBSE 2026-27 topics. Classes 6-9 follow the current NCERT science series; Classes 11-12 follow CBSE Physics 2026-27. Class 5 entries are foundational app activities. A small number of established supplementary lab topics are retained.

experiments.title: Light and Shadows
experiments.description: Move a light source, object and screen to investigate shadow size, shape and direction.

experiments.title: Simple Machines
experiments.description: Explore levers, pulleys and inclined planes by changing load, effort and position.

experiments.title: Sound and Vibrations
experiments.description: Change vibration speed and strength to explore how sound is produced and how pitch and loudness change.

experiments.title: Exploring Magnets
experiments.description: Move magnets, a compass and magnetic materials to investigate poles, attraction, repulsion and magnetic fields.

experiments.title: Measurement of Length
experiments.description: Use a virtual ruler and measuring tools to measure objects, compare units and understand measurement accuracy.

experiments.title: Motion and Measurement
experiments.description: Change distance and time, compare uniform and non-uniform motion, and read simple motion graphs.

experiments.title: Temperature and Its Measurement
experiments.description: Use virtual thermometers to compare temperatures and observe how readings change during heating and cooling.

experiments.title: Beyond Earth: Solar System Explorer
experiments.description: Explore the Sun, Earth, Moon and planets, and change their relative positions to understand basic astronomical patterns.

experiments.title: Electricity: Circuits and Their Components
experiments.description: Build a working circuit by connecting cells, wires, switches and bulbs; test open and closed circuits.

experiments.title: Heat Transfer in Nature
experiments.description: Compare conduction, convection and radiation using adjustable materials and temperature readings.

experiments.title: Measurement of Time and Motion
experiments.description: Change pendulum length and count oscillations to compare time period and periodic motion.

experiments.title: Light: Shadows and Reflection
experiments.description: Move a light source, object and plane mirror to explore shadow formation and the law of reflection.

experiments.title: Earth, Moon and the Sun
experiments.description: Control the positions and motion of the Earth, Moon and Sun to explore day, night and lunar phases.

experiments.title: Electricity: Magnetic and Heating Effects
experiments.description: Change current, coil turns and resistance to explore heating, magnetic fields and electromagnets.

experiments.title: Exploring Forces: Friction and Motion
experiments.description: Change the applied force and surface to investigate friction, balanced forces and motion.

experiments.title: Pressure, Winds, Storms and Cyclones
experiments.description: Change fluid depth, density and air-pressure differences to explore pressure, winds and storm formation.

experiments.title: Sound Propagation and Medium
experiments.description: Explore how sound travels through solids, liquids and gases and compare the effects of different media.

experiments.title: Light: Mirrors and Lenses
experiments.description: Move mirrors, convex and concave lenses, objects and screens to investigate image formation.

experiments.title: Keeping Time with the Skies
experiments.description: Explore repeating sky patterns and use a simple celestial-motion model to understand timekeeping.

experiments.title: Describing Motion Around Us
experiments.description: Change position, speed and direction and interpret distance-time and velocity-time graphs.

experiments.title: How Forces Affect Motion
experiments.description: Apply balanced and unbalanced forces and observe inertia, acceleration and action-reaction pairs.

experiments.title: Work, Energy and Simple Machines
experiments.description: Change force, displacement and height to explore work, energy transfer and mechanical advantage.

experiments.title: Sound Waves: Characteristics and Applications
experiments.description: Adjust frequency, amplitude and medium to explore sound waves, echoes, reflection and applications.

experiments.title: Density and Archimedes' Principle
experiments.description: Change object mass and volume, then observe floating, sinking, buoyant force and displaced fluid.

experiments.title: Light: Reflection and Refraction
experiments.description: Explore plane and spherical mirrors, lenses, image formation, refraction and prism-based dispersion in one optics workspace.

experiments.title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
experiments.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
experiments.description: Explore eye accommodation, common vision defects and correction, dispersion and atmospheric optical effects.

experiments.title: Electricity: Ohm's Law and Circuits
experiments.description: Adjust voltage and resistance, build series and parallel circuits, and observe current, voltage and power.

experiments.title: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
experiments.description: Change current direction and coil turns to explore magnetic fields, electromagnets, motors and generators.

experiments.title: Units and Measurements: Vernier Calipers and Screw Gauge
experiments.description: Take virtual measurements, find least count and compare precision, accuracy and measurement error.

experiments.title: Motion in a Straight Line
experiments.description: Change initial velocity and acceleration and investigate displacement, velocity and motion graphs.

experiments.title: Motion in a Plane
experiments.description: Adjust vector magnitude and direction to explore vector addition, projectile motion and circular motion.

experiments.title: Laws of Motion: Forces and Inclined Plane
experiments.description: Adjust mass, applied force, friction and slope to study Newton's laws and free-body forces.

experiments.title: Work, Energy and Power
experiments.description: Change force, displacement, height and time to compare work, kinetic energy, potential energy and power.

experiments.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
experiments.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
experiments.description: Move masses and change torque to explore centre of mass, angular acceleration and rotational equilibrium.

experiments.title: Gravitation
experiments.description: Change masses and separation to explore gravitational force, orbital motion and variation of gravitational acceleration.

experiments.title: Mechanical Properties of Solids: Hooke's Law
experiments.description: Add loads to a spring and observe extension, elastic limit and the force-extension relationship.

experiments.title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
experiments.description: Explore pressure, buoyancy, viscosity, surface tension and capillary action using virtual fluid setups.

experiments.title: Thermal Properties of Matter
experiments.description: Change heat input and material properties to explore expansion, calorimetry and heat transfer.

experiments.title: Thermodynamics
experiments.description: Control heat and work in a model system to explore internal energy and thermodynamic processes.

experiments.title: Kinetic Theory
experiments.description: Change gas temperature, volume and particle number to observe molecular motion and pressure.

experiments.title: Oscillations
experiments.description: Adjust mass, spring constant and pendulum length to explore simple harmonic motion and energy exchange.

experiments.title: Waves
experiments.description: Change frequency, amplitude, wavelength and tension to explore travelling waves, standing waves, resonance and sound.

experiments.title: Electric Charges and Fields
experiments.description: Move charges and explore Coulomb force, electric field lines, superposition and electric dipoles.

experiments.title: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
experiments.description: Explore potential maps, potential difference, capacitor geometry and stored energy.

experiments.title: Current Electricity: Meter Bridge and Resistivity
experiments.description: Build circuits, adjust resistance and use a meter bridge balance point to calculate unknown resistance and resistivity.

experiments.title: Moving Charges and Magnetism
experiments.description: Change charge velocity and current direction to explore magnetic force, fields and motion in a magnetic field.

experiments.title: Magnetism and Matter
experiments.description: Explore bar magnets, magnetic dipoles, field patterns and the response of magnetic materials.

experiments.title: Electromagnetic Induction
experiments.description: Move a magnet or coil and change turns and speed to observe induced emf and Lenz's law.

experiments.title: Alternating Current
experiments.description: Change frequency and circuit components to explore AC waveforms, reactance, impedance and resonance.

experiments.title: Electromagnetic Waves
experiments.description: Explore how electric and magnetic fields propagate and compare the electromagnetic spectrum.

experiments.title: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
experiments.description: Explore image formation by mirrors and lenses, focal length, prism deviation and basic optical instruments.

experiments.title: Wave Optics
experiments.description: Change slit separation and wavelength to explore interference, diffraction and polarization.

experiments.title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
experiments.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
experiments.description: Change light frequency and intensity to investigate photoelectric emission and de Broglie wavelength.

experiments.title: Atoms
experiments.description: Explore atomic spectra and simple atomic models by changing energy levels and transitions.

experiments.title: Nuclei
experiments.description: Compare nuclear size, binding energy and radioactive decay using a safe model simulation.

experiments.title: Semiconductor Electronics
experiments.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
experiments.description: Change diode bias and circuit components to observe current-voltage behaviour and simple semiconductor circuits.
